newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares plunge at close on crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares plunge at close on crackdown.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices continued to plunge on Tuesday, closing near their limit-down levels of 10 percent due to Beijing's crackdown on the stock markets, traders said.
The A index plummeted 41.69 points or 9.99 percent to 375.51 points and the B index dived 12.79 points, or 9.51 percent, to 121.64 points. The indices also closed limit-down on Monday.
Most shares hit the daily limit-down of 10 percent shortly after the opening, as on Monday, and stayed there for the whole session, brokers said.
"Few small investors are willing to buy after Monday's nosedive," a broker said.

"Some bargain hunters were seen cautiously buying some high-priced issues, which at one point stood above their limit-down levels. But they were eventually pushed down by heavy selling," the broker said.
"Institutions largely stayed on the sidelines to monitor the market's performance," an analyst said.
Turnover in Shenzhen expanded greatly on Tuesday, with A share turnover at 2.78 billion yuan against Monday's 693.64 million yuan and B turnover at HK$133.63 million against HK$15.48 million.

The market will continue to fall sharply on Wednesday as sentiment has been destroyed by Beijing's crackdown, brokers said. But some issues with solid earnings record still stand a chance of being targeted by light bargain hunting, they added.
On the B share market, SEZ Real Estate traded the most on volume of 3.14 million shares, sliding HK$0.42 to HK$3.77.
Diesel engine maker Changchai lost HK$0.52 to HK$5.23 on trade of 3.13 million shares.
Shenzhen A share market leader Shenzhen Development Bank fell 1.69 yuan to 15.17 yuan on the session's most active trade of 46.37 million shares.

Petrochemical concern Hubei Tianfa Enterprises (Group) Co Ltd, which listed 28.60 million A shares in Shenzhen on Tuesday, ended the session at 15.09 yuan against an offer price of one yuan per share in 1990.
The 10 percent limit on daily movement policy does not apply to counters on their first trading day.
